verdict.rationale: QuickBooks' official MCP server supports restricting which tool categories are registered and can suppress write operations via QUICKBOOKS_DISABLE_WRITE, giving a practical least-privilege mechanism for agent access, and OAuth 2.0 client libraries handle standard token issuance/refresh. However, there's no evidence of fine-grained, per-scope OAuth credential issuance (e.g., read-only vs. specific-entity scopes) at the API/auth-server level beyond the coarse standard QBO OAuth scope. Missing for 10: documented granular OAuth scopes for agents, first-party guidance on issuing narrowly-scoped tokens, and independent confirmation the write-suppression flag is enforced server-side rather than just client-side.
